M O R E   M A I L ! !

   August, 1992      Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Alan D. Cox..........03    07

 Derek Morgan.........10    16

 Malcolm Goodman......17    19

 L.G. Baumann.........20    22

 W.A. Yates...........27    30

 Malcolm Perry........31    39

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Alan D. Cox, DYFED

Dear Brian,

I decided that it was time I did
something about reducing your
workload so I have invested in a
second-hand copy of TASWORD2. I
must confess that the fact that
it only cost me `5, and I also
got a copy of OUTWRITE! for `6,
helped. At the moment I am
struggling a bit, but I hope I
shall be reasonably fluent
before long, although whether I
shall ever be truly tri-lingual
is open to doubt.

As an aside, I notice that the
manual for TASWORD says that it
is copyright and is sold subject

to the condition that it is
not.....resold... I must say I
find this odd - surely they
really cannot object to resale
of the original? After all, if I
buy a book which is copyright,
there is no reason of which I am
aware why I cannot sell it once
I have finished with it.


First, abject apologies to
Messrs Seddon and Smith, and
anyone else who had the same
problem with OUTDEXMERG. It
worked when I sent it to you
but clearly there are conditions
when it doesn't. I will sort it
out as soon as I can, although I
cannot be certain of doing it by
next month.

On 'NANOOK', I gather you want
to drop it now and I would not
dissent - you got some inter-
esting comments which presumably
was the main aim. I'd only want
to resolve the 'centrifugal'
issue.If you are at the equator,
for example, then Newton's laws
show that you will travel on a
straight line tangential to the
Earth's surface unless there is
a force acting on you, and this
force, which is part of the pull
due to gravity, is towards the
centre of the Earth i.e.
centripetal.

(I would have underlined some
parts of the words if I knew how
to do it easily, as I can with
WORDMASTER!)

I note your reference to Alex
Kinch and the fair that he is
planning. As I used to live in
the area, I can point out that
you should have referred to West
Wickham, not Wycombe - they are
by no means the same place.

Do you know of anyone who has a
Disciple or a Plus D and disk
drive for sale?

I hope that your financial
crisis sorts itself out quickly

        All best wishes,

           Alan D.Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

I assume Tasman meant Tasword
must not be resold commercially
in some way (how I'm not sure).
There can be no restriction on
selling an original piece of
software as secondhand privately
like, as you say, any book.

I don't think I wanted to "drop"
NANOOK (except down an 8,000
mile hole to simulate zero
gravity) but assumed we'd pretty
well exhausted my futile attempt
to make money from those dieting
Eskimos. I think I now see what
you mean by centripetal.This now
seems to me that there are TWO
forces acting - both centrifugal
(to fling out) and centripetal
(to pull in).

If the Earth had no atmosphere
and was rotating about 18 times
faster then people at the
equator would feel a centrifugal
force of about 1 gravity exactly
matching the Earth's gravity so
would be weightless - floating
effortlessly along the Earth's
surface. Cars would do about
500 million miles to the gallon
(assuming they carried oxygen).
You wouldn't need a car. You
could just take a deep breath,
jump up and come down two miles
away. Think of the bus fares you
would save going to work.

Funnily enough, NANOOK would
still be as heavy as ever and I
guess one could jump to the
North Pole but not jump back.

That could be a serious problem
for mankind actually. All those
taking a wrong turn would end up
at the poles but not be able to
leap back. The ice would begin
to melt from the impact of many
millions of people leaping about
trying to get back to Zanzibar,
California and Milton Keynes
(actually no,surely none of them
would bother trying to get back
to Milton Keynes).

On second thoughts, when they
first leapt to the poles they
would be descending under full
Earth gravity and be splattered
all over the snow - especially
with no atmosphere to slow the
fall. I shall worry about this.
At least the greenhouse effect
would no longer be a problem.

From: D.R. Morgan,
      18 Mill lane, Glenburn Rd,
      Old Skelmersdale,
      Lancashire, WN8 8RH
      (0695)31163

Dear Brian and Ron,

I have been sent some excellent
software from one of your
regular contributors, Dylan
Kevin Hall (Colony Software), of
Australia, to sell for him. I
have been selling his Sam Sound
Digitiser program for some time
in the small ads, and it is
still selling well.

I got my knuckles rapped by
Dylan for the poor advert that I
sent in and more so the fact

that I must have led readers to
believe that it was my program
and not his. I must apologise to
readers and Dylan if this was
the case.

Now, onto his new software.

THE MOUSE DISK. This compilation
of programs is for use with the
SAMCo mouse. Dylan sent the disk
to SAMCo as an alternative to
the disk sent out with the
mouse, but after a few changes
to the disk he has decided it
was so good that he would sell
it himself.

The disk contains the mouse
information and basic mouse
driver with a difference.

The games are PacMan, Space
Invaders and Nuke. There is also
a free version of Flash which
makes full use of the mouse, ie
Load, Save, etc.

COLOURING BOOK

An excellent program that lets
you colour screens, by using 15
colour pens. There are no less
than 30 Turtles screens on disk.
The program has an auto colour
mode so you can let the program
do it for you, or after you have
coloured the picture you can
re-colour it with the auto
function. The erase mode will
un-colour the screen for you to
start again. Controls are Mouse,
Joystick and keys.

SAM JIGSAW Disk
Another excellent program - it
kept my nephews quiet for hours.
There 42 screens on disk that
are re-arranged to form a jigsaw
(not a 'slidy' game). There are
four modes of play, from easy to
hard, and to make things a
little interesting some screens
have Palette scrolling. Controls
are Mouse, Joystick and Keys.

All programs are `5.00 including
postage. I am trying to get
Dylan to produce a free demo
disk that's free if you send a
disk and return postage.

From Paul Skinner of New Zealand
comes the first WIMP's utility
program that I have seen on SAM.

This is a wonderful program and
a must for anyone like me who
likes to keep his disk in an
orderly fashion. The program is
best used with MasterDos, but
will work just as easily with
Samdos and still show sub-
directories. 1 & 2 MB memory and
two disk drives are also catered
for. There are still one or two
extra things that Paul is
adding, like remaining sub-
directories.

Coming soon from Colony Software
is some new hardware for SAM - a
three way Joystick Splitter
Interface. The JSI, as it is
known in Australia, has a
Kempston compatible joystick
port, so no more problems with

Spectrum games being joystick
incompatible. The JSI also has a
Reset and NMI button included,
and just in case you were
wondering how you could fit
another interface on. Don't
worry because it has an
expansion through port fitted,
and all housed in the standard
interface box.

Help, I am looking for a program
on SAM or Spectrum to be used
for working out the time in
pigeon racing, over distances.
If anyone has such a program can
they please get in touch with
me. I will refund any postage.

             Derek

Brian Cavers to Derek Morgan


Thanks, Derek.

Regarding your inquiry about
obtaining OUTLET in Australia
by standing order, the answer is
yes but the price will be `3.50
to help cover the extra postage.

Please ask us for one of our
pre-prepared standing order
forms if you definitely want to
go ahead as we need to reference
it to our system.
                        - Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Your editorial in last month's
OUTLET made depressing reading.
I hope it was a one-off blip in
sales as I believe that there
are many who need a monthly
"fix" of OUTLET.

Now, onto your reply about how
to "interrogate" what has been
assigned to numeric or string
variables.Your suggestion's fine
for numerics, but if you let V$=
"hello" then use V$ in the INPUT
prompt, then the answer you get
is "V$" and not "hello". Try it,
and you will realise why I set
the problem in the first place.
I believe it still remains a
good programming puzzle.

Lastly, your comments about code
location in the SAM. One
possible answer is the 'LOCATOR'
routine published by John Pitts
in Issue One of 'SOFTRIX'. It is
not PD so if it's what you want
then you'll need to contact him.

           Regards,

            Malcolm

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman


Ah! - I see now what you mean!
If the INPUT string variable is
the same as the one you want to
investigate then it will destroy
it! Mr. L.G. Baumann spotted my
mistake too so I will reply more
fully on this whole puzzle after
the next letter.

Thanks for the LOCATOR info. It
is not quite what I had in mind
but was of interest anyway. Pity
this routine isn't PD as it does
severely limit its usefulness!

                        - Brian

From: L. G. Baumann, STH. AFRICA

Dear Brian,

Malcolm Goodman raised a problem
on variables in your OUTLETTERS
of July 1992 to which you gave a
possible solution.Unfortunately,
your suggested program destroys
the value already held in the
string V$.

I think it is necessary to park
the value of V$ in a temporary
home and restore it to its value
later.

Perhaps the following changes to
your listing will be of some
help (assuming the variables
have already all been declared):

 10 LET temp = VAL V$: INPUT
    "Variable? ";V$
 20 IF V$ = "V$" THEN LET V$ =
    STR$ temp
 30 IF V$ (LEN V$ = "$" THEN
    PRINT VAL$ V$: LET V$ =
    STR$ temp: GO TO 10
 40 PRINT VAL V$: LET V$ =  STR$
    temp: GO TO 10

I will be interested to see the
other solutions that will be
given.

          L.G.Baumann

Brian Cavers to L.G. Baumann

Yes,I see my mistake but you are
making the assumption that the
string variables contain only
numerals whereas they may have
text which would crash with your
solution with "variable not
found". The idea of storing the
variable first seems promising
though. Perhaps one could POKE
it into memory, character by
character and then read it back.
However, this would be slow with
a very large string and care
would have to be taken not to
POKE memory used by something
else - not ideal for a universal
solution as this wants to be.
This is a good puzzle and I have
one more possible solution...

First, for other readers who may
not have seen Malcolm Goodman's
letter last month, the puzzle is
to write a BASIC routine that
would let you enter the name of
any of (previously-declared) 26
numeric variables and 26 strings
for each letter of the alphabet
and have it printed up, e.g.,you
would enter X and it would print
99 (if x=99) or enter Z$ and it
would print "hello" (if z$ is
"hello").

After Malcolm's and your letters
this month I went back to the
wording of Malcolm's first
challenge and noticed he didn't
state INPUT as such. I began to
wonder what other ways are there
of entering anything into the
computer from the keyboard...

I can only think of INKEY$ but
it would still seem to need a
string variable to store its
value. Of course, SAM has GET as
well but the same applies.

Incidentally on SAM, my previous
solution would work if the INPUT
used a 2-letter string variable
name like VV$ or a long weird
name like QZOGKUQQ$ would let it
work with any reasonable name.
However, for this puzzle I am
sticking to a universal solution
that will work on either SAM or
Spectrum.

I've been racking my brains and
I think I have a way to store
INKEY$ without a variable but I
have not tried it so here goes..

10 DECLARE VARIABLES ETC...
20 CLS : PRINT "VARIABLE? "
20 PAUSE 0:PRINT INKEY$;
30 PAUSE 0:PRINT INKEY$
40 IF SCREEN$(1,1)=" " THEN
   PRINT VAL SCREEN$(1,0): STOP
60 IF SCREEN$(1,0)="A" THEN
   PRINT A$
70 IF SCREEN$(1,0)="B" THEN
   PRINT B$
   ETC. ETC...

As I was typing this I could see
my original plan would not work
out. I had hoped to use say...
PRINT VAL$(SCREEN$(1,0)+ SCREEN$
(1,1)) but the SCREEN$ bug stops
any string slicing without first
storing in a variable so needing
at least TWO string variables to
get more than one character off
the screen.

I must admit I'm stuck for the
moment. I suppose one could POKE
the BASIC line directly to alter
a PRINT statement.

I'll give it some more thought.
Anyone else care to try!!??

                        - Brian

From: W.A. Yates, CHORLEY

Dear Ron,

Many thanks for the information
reference the printer printing a
question mark down the left side
of the letters. I have changed
the dip switches to the American
code. I can now print the ` sign
as long as I don't forget to
type in the POKE @ 6,1 before I
start to type, it is now as you
said Press symbol shift and the
hash sign, and it prints out the
pound sign with no question mark
on the left.

I have waited a long time for
the All Formats Computer Show to
come to the north, but I was

very disappointed. Out of about
25 stalls there was only the
Format magazine to represent the
Spectrum and this one stall was
also running the SAM computer.
What a let down. I won't be
going to any more shows. If that
was a sample of other shows and
the cost of `3.00 with a ticket
from Format - it was a rip off
to say the least.

Well, I won't go on as it gets
my back up. At least I can load
my OUTLET disc and have a read
and try the programs and break
into them and see how they work
even if I don't understand them.
And for `3.50 I can keep
loading them in and I can see
the show again and again and if

I want I can go to number one
and go through them all again,
which I often do. Now that's
what I call a bargain, so keep
up the good work.

       Yours sincerely,

          W.A. Yates

Brian Cavers to W.A. Yates

It does sound like Spectrum and
SAM presence is declining at
recent fairs. I heard the more
recent Birmingham Fair only had
two SAM stalls. Perhaps I had
better mention this in future
LOOKOUT fair fixtures as I don't
like to think OUTLET readers'
expectations might be raised too
high. Meanwhile, I'd still very
much appreciate anyone who does
visit fairs to keep us informed
of attendance, support etc. so
we can all keep in touch.

                        - Brian

From: M. Perry, KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Brian and Ron,

In answer to the question from
Mark Longthorn on the +D drive
connector, the pin layout is as
follows - also true for Disciple
and SAM external drive adaptor
(except, I believe, D1/2 select
is different in that the drive
is left as D1 and the select is
done in the interface).

Looking at the rear of the +D
the pins are numbered from right
to left with all odd numbers on
top and even numbers on bottom.

33 31 ........ 5 3 1
34 32 ........ 6 4 2

All the top row, odd numbers are
EARTHS ( 0V )

On the bottom row, all even
numbers are as follows. Note NU
= not used. "+" represents +D is
outputting data or a signal to
control drive and "-" means it
is a drive status signal or data
into +D.
    2   NU
    4   NU
    6   NU
    8 - INDEX
   10 + DRIVE ONE SELECT
   12 + DRIVE TWO SELECT
   14   NU
   16 + MOTOR ON
   18 + STEP DIRECTION
   20 + STEP SIGNAL
   22 + DATA OUT, WRITE

   24 + WRITE GATE
   26 - TRACK ZERO
   28   NU
   30 - DATA IN, READ
   32 + SELECT SIDE
   34   NU

The plug on the rear of the
drive is the same format as
above except that pins marked NU
carry signals that the +D does
not use e.g. pin 14 can be drive
3 select. Obviously, direction
of signals "+" represents into
drive and "-" signal out of
drive.

The pins are at 5V level for
"off" or not selected and pulled
down to 0V for function active
or select.

The 26 pin printer plug is also
numbered as above and
connections are:-
1, strobe. All odd 3 to 17 inc.
data bits 0 to 7 res. 21 busy
All even 2 to 22 inc.earth (0V).
Odds 19 to 25 inc and 24 & 26
are not used.

DIRECTORIES. The mention of CAT
1 "x" is the selective directory
listing form.Not well documented
as I recall in the handbooks.


A specific name such as "TEST"
would only list the program
"TEST" if there is one. "TEST*"
would list all files starting
with TEST such as TEST1,TEST2
TESTING and so on.

The "?" can also be used as for
example "??R*" would only list
files that have"R" as the third
letter. Just to recap on "*" and
"?" The "?" means "this can be
any character", the "*" means
"this character can be anything
and any following are ignored".
That is why ERASE "*" wipes the
entire disc and the characters
"*" and "?" can cause problems
if used in file names.
E.g. say a file name of "*this"
was put on disc. now try and
erase with "*this": disaster - a
blank disc! Remember the rule
"*" this can be anything and
ignore everything after so erase
all files with any first char-
acter and ignore any trailing
characters.

"?this" would only erase "*this"
and any other 5 letter name with
"THIS" as the last 4 characters.
Incidentally,on a blank disc,try
SAVE d1 "*ONE". Now try and save
"*TWO" It asks if you want to
overwrite "*ONE"! There must be
a use for this somewhere but
indicates why the * and ? should
not be used in file names.

I have recently found that the
5V supply to my SAM is somewhat
unstable and falls towards 4.5V
on disc operation, also varied
due to poor connection of the
power input 6 pin plug. The
obvious visible signs are flick-
ering and changes of brightness
of screen, there could well be
less obvious effects.

The disc control IC to name one
is stated as 5V +/- 5% which
gives it a lower limit of 4.75V
the 5V rail is going below this
specification. Is this a reason
for some of the drive problems I
wonder?

What other ICs or even drives
are being expected to run with a
5V rail that goes below their
specification limits I ask. I
know from experience certain
drives failed to work reliably
if the supply fell below about
4.7V.

I believe the volt drop could be
due to the somewhat thin
multicore cable between PSU and
computer.

This fall in voltage on load
would be even worse if things
such as audio amps, card cage
without extra PSU and etc.  are
also drawing on the 5V rail of
SAM. As my machine is still both
under guarantee and the subject
of a dispute, I refrained from
checking to see how stable the
5V is in the PSU itself to prove
the cable theory. It would be
interesting though to check the
5V supply on a machine that is
playing up and running it from a
more stable supply. Note I am
not recommending you go poking
voltages into SAM 'cos as a
certain person in a TV show says
"they don't like it up 'em they
don't " unless you know what you
are doing.       - Malcolm Perry.

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

I don't think I realized that
ERASE "*THIS" would erase every-
thing on the disc! I don't use
"*" in filenames although I
don't think I make a conscious
effort not to do so - rather
it's just not a symbol I would
gener- ally use in a filename.
Let's hope I remember!

One other symbol that has caused
me minor inconvenience is the
"/" character.This has been used
by readers in filenames of text
files and Masterdos doesn't like
it of course. I forget the error
message but it does prevent one
loading them without SAMDOS!
                       - Brian.

Dear Brian and Ron,

In answer to the question from Mark Longthorn on the +D drive connector, the pin layout is as follows - also true for Disciple and SAM external drive adaptor (except, I believe, D1/2 select is different in that the drive is left as D1 and the select is done in the interface).

Looking at the rear of the +D the pins are numbered from right to left with all odd numbers on top and even numbers on bottom.

```text
33 31 ........ 5 3 1
34 32 ........ 6 4 2
```

All the top row, odd numbers are EARTHS ( 0V )

On the bottom row, all even numbers are as follows. Note NU = not used. "+" represents +D is outputting data or a signal to control drive and "-" means it is a drive status signal or data into +D.

```text
    2   NU
    4   NU
    6   NU
```

8 - INDEX 10 + DRIVE ONE SELECT 12 + DRIVE TWO SELECT

```text
   14   NU
```

16 + MOTOR ON 18 + STEP DIRECTION 20 + STEP SIGNAL 22 + DATA OUT, WRITE

24 + WRITE GATE 26 - TRACK ZERO

```text
   28   NU
```

30 - DATA IN, READ 32 + SELECT SIDE

```text
   34   NU
```

The plug on the rear of the drive is the same format as above except that pins marked NU carry signals that the +D does not use e.g. pin 14 can be drive 3 select. Obviously, direction of signals "+" represents into drive and "-" signal out of drive.

The pins are at 5V level for "off" or not selected and pulled down to 0V for function active or select.

The 26 pin printer plug is also numbered as above and connections are:- 1, strobe. All odd 3 to 17 inc. data bits 0 to 7 res. 21 busy All even 2 to 22 inc.earth (0V). Odds 19 to 25 inc and 24 & 26 are not used.

DIRECTORIES. The mention of CAT 1 "x" is the selective directory listing form.Not well documented as I recall in the handbooks.

A specific name such as "TEST" would only list the program "TEST" if there is one. "TEST*" would list all files starting with TEST such as TEST1,TEST2 TESTING and so on.

The "?" can also be used as for example "??R*" would only list files that have"R" as the third letter. Just to recap on "*" and "?" The "?" means "this can be any character", the "*" means "this character can be anything and any following are ignored". That is why ERASE "*" wipes the entire disc and the characters "*" and "?" can cause problems if used in file names. E.g. say a file name of "*this" was put on disc. now try and erase with "*this": disaster - a blank disc! Remember the rule "*" this can be anything and ignore everything after so erase all files with any first char- acter and ignore any trailing characters.

"?this" would only erase "*this" and any other 5 letter name with "THIS" as the last 4 characters. Incidentally,on a blank disc,try SAVE d1 "*ONE". Now try and save "*TWO" It asks if you want to overwrite "*ONE"! There must be a use for this somewhere but indicates why the * and ? should not be used in file names.

I have recently found that the 5V supply to my SAM is somewhat unstable and falls towards 4.5V on disc operation, also varied due to poor connection of the power input 6 pin plug. The obvious visible signs are flick- ering and changes of brightness of screen, there could well be less obvious effects.

The disc control IC to name one is stated as 5V +/- 5% which gives it a lower limit of 4.75V the 5V rail is going below this specification. Is this a reason for some of the drive problems I wonder?

What other ICs or even drives are being expected to run with a 5V rail that goes below their specification limits I ask. I know from experience certain drives failed to work reliably if the supply fell below about 4.7V.

I believe the volt drop could be due to the somewhat thin multicore cable between PSU and computer.

This fall in voltage on load would be even worse if things such as audio amps, card cage without extra PSU and etc.  are also drawing on the 5V rail of SAM. As my machine is still both under guarantee and the subject of a dispute, I refrained from checking to see how stable the 5V is in the PSU itself to prove the cable theory. It would be interesting though to check the 5V supply on a machine that is playing up and running it from a more stable supply. Note I am not recommending you go poking voltages into SAM 'cos as a certain person in a TV show says "they don't like it up 'em they don't " unless you know what you are doing.       - Malcolm Perry.

От: M. Perry, KIDDERMINSTER

Уважаемые Brian и Ron!

В ответ на вопрос Mark Longthorn о разъёме дисковода интерфейса +D: цоколёвка выводов следующая — она верна также для Disciple и адаптера внешнего дисковода SAM (за исключением того, что, как мне кажется, выбор D1/D2 отличается: дисковод остаётся сконфигурирован как D1, а переключение выполняется внутри интерфейса).

Если смотреть на заднюю панель +D, контакты нумеруются справа налево: нечётные сверху, чётные снизу.

```text
33 31 ........ 5 3 1
34 32 ........ 6 4 2
```

Весь верхний ряд, нечётные номера — ЗЕМЛЯ (0V).

В нижнем ряду все чётные номера распределены следующим образом. Примечание: NU = не используется (not used). Знак «+» означает, что +D выдаёт данные или сигнал управления на дисковод, а знак «-» означает, что это сигнал состояния дисковода или входные данные в +D.

```text
 2    NU
 4    NU
 6    NU
 8  - INDEX
10  + DRIVE ONE SELECT
12  + DRIVE TWO SELECT
14    NU
16  + MOTOR ON
18  + STEP DIRECTION
20  + STEP SIGNAL
22  + DATA OUT, WRITE
24  + WRITE GATE
26  - TRACK ZERO
28    NU
30  - DATA IN, READ
32  + SELECT SIDE
34    NU
```

Разъём на задней панели дисковода имеет тот же формат, что и выше, за исключением того, что контакты, помеченные NU, несут сигналы, которые +D не использует (например, контакт 14 может быть выбором третьего дисковода — Drive 3 Select). Естественно, направление сигналов: «+» — сигнал идёт в дисковод, а «-» — сигнал выходит из дисковода.

Уровень сигналов на контактах составляет 5 В для пассивного («off») или невыбранного состояния и притягивается к 0 В для активации функции или выбора.

26-контактный разъём для принтера пронумерован аналогичным образом, и подключения следующие:  
1 — Strobe. Все нечётные с 3 по 17 включительно — биты данных от 0 до 7 соответственно. 21 — Busy. Все чётные с 2 по 22 включительно — земля (0V). Нечётные с 19 по 25 включительно, а также 24 и 26 не используются.

КАТАЛОГИ. Упоминание команды `CAT 1 "x"` относится к выборочному выводу каталога. Насколько я помню, это не слишком хорошо задокументировано в руководствах.

Конкретное имя, например «TEST», выведет только программу «TEST», если таковая существует. «TEST*» выдаст список всех файлов, начинающихся на TEST, таких как TEST1, TEST2, TESTING и так далее.

Символ «?» также можно использовать: к примеру, «??R*» выведет только те файлы, у которых третья буква — «R». Напомню правила для «*» и «?»: «?» означает «здесь может быть любой одиночный символ», а «*» означает «здесь может быть любой символ, а все последующие игнорируются». Вот почему `ERASE "*"` стирает диск целиком, а символы «*» и «?» могут вызвать проблемы, если использовать их в именах файлов.

Например, скажем, на диск записан файл с именем «*this». А теперь попробуйте стереть его командой `ERASE "*this"`: катастрофа — пустой диск! Помните правило: «*» означает любой символ и игнорирование всего, что идёт после, то есть удаляются все файлы с любым первым символом и отбрасываются все последующие.

Команда `ERASE "?this"` удалит только «*this» и любое другое 5-буквенное имя, оканчивающееся на «THIS». Кстати, попробуйте на чистом диске сделать `SAVE d1 "*ONE"`. А теперь попробуйте сохранить `SAVE "*TWO"`. Система спросит, хотите ли вы перезаписать «*ONE»! Где-то этому, должно быть, можно найти применение, но это наглядно показывает, почему не следует использовать * и ? в именах файлов.

Недавно я обнаружил, что линия питания 5V в моём SAM довольно нестабильна и проседает почти до 4.5V при работе дисковода, а также «гуляет» из-за плохого контакта в 6-контактном разъёме питания. Очевидные внешние признаки — мерцание и изменение яркости экрана, но могут быть и менее заметные последствия.

Для микросхемы контроллера дисковода, к примеру, заявлено питание 5V +/- 5%, что даёт нижний предел в 4.75V — а шина 5V проседает ниже этой спецификации. Уж не в этом ли кроется причина некоторых проблем с дисководами?

Каким ещё микросхемам или даже дисководам приходится работать с шиной 5V, падающей ниже допустимых для них пределов, спрашивается? По опыту я знаю, что некоторые дисководы переставали надёжно работать, если напряжение питания опускалось ниже примерно 4.7V.

Я полагаю, что падение напряжения может быть вызвано довольно тонким многожильным кабелем между блоком питания и компьютером.

Это падение напряжения под нагрузкой станет ещё сильнее, если такие устройства, как аудиоусилители, корзина расширения (card cage) без дополнительного БП и т.д., также будут питаться от 5-вольтовой шины SAM. Поскольку моя машина всё ещё на гарантии и является предметом спора, я воздержался от проверки того, насколько стабильны 5V в самом БП, чтобы подтвердить теорию о кабеле. Однако было бы любопытно проверить шину 5V на сбоящей машине и запитать её от более стабильного источника. Заметьте, я не рекомендую вам лезть с напряжениями внутрь SAM — как говорит один персонаж в телешоу, «they don't like it up 'em they don't», если только вы точно не знаете, что делаете.
